answer.evidence: Most first-layer units (0, 3-7, 9-16, 19, 21, 22, 24-26, 28, 30, 31) have unstructured weights inside roughly the ±70 initialisation range. None of them shows a compact high-magnitude patch such as a corner marker or band. The clearly trained units are of two kinds. (1) Units 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29 have broad positive weights over the central region, roughly rows 4-20 and cols 4-20, with values up to about 96. Traced through W2 and W3 they push the logit positive: summed W2×W3 products are about +17.6k for unit 1, +9.6k for unit 8, +10.9k for unit 20 and +32k for unit 18. Unit 2 is slightly negative (about -2.6k) and unit 29 is near zero (+0.7k). (2) Units 17 and 23 have strongly negative centres (down to about -97) and positive periphery. For unit 17 the positive weights are top, bottom and right; for unit 23 they are top and left. Both push the logit negative (about -2.4k and -6.0k). Unit 27 is broadly positive with a heavier periphery and pushes positive (about +6k). Unit 23's top-row band (rows 0-3) is somewhat asymmetric, but similar top and bottom positivity appears in units 17 and 27. It is accompanied by a negative centre, so it reads as a centre-versus-surround contrast rather than an isolated artifact detector. No localized, label-tied patch outside the nodule region was found.
answer.main_feature: The model scores bright, large or dense tissue in the central region (the nodule size and density) as malignant. Configurations with a dark centre and bright surrounding tissue (small or faint nodules) push toward benign.
